name: anime sound edits
summary: A sound edit is a 8.5-11.3 s loop of a song's most percussive hook (4 bars) in which every shot contributes ONE audible hit from its own anime audio (punch, click, clap, stomp, gunshot, cork pop...), and that hit lands on a song onset: clip hit vs nearest song onset |dt| median 9 ms, 75 % within 25 ms, 78 % within 40 ms (55 hits, 4 waveform-aligned references).

The CUT does not sit on the beat: it comes a pre-roll BEFORE the hit (median 140 ms, p25 82, p75 210 ms = 2-5 frames at 24 fps) so the viewer sees the wind-up; only 10 % of cuts are within 40 ms of a song onset.

Shots are short and even: median 9 frames at 24 fps (0.375 s), p10 6, p90 13 frames; 1.6-3.2 cuts/s; 4-8 cuts per bar; the cut pattern repeats bar to bar (75-100 % of cuts repeat a 16th position of the previous bar) because it follows the song's riff.

Picture is plain: 112 of 114 cuts are hard cuts (two short cross-dissolves of 2 and 3 frames, both in FB15TNFAHVU), no added camera moves (median zoom per shot 0.0 %, 5/119 shots move > 4 % and those are the source's own camera), native speed (no slow motion, no ramps, no frame blending), no grade, no text except a faint creator watermark.

Audio: the song runs untouched at constant level (no ducking; gain change after a cut 0.0-1.7 dB) with the clip sounds on top: each hit peaks +5 dB (p25 +3, p75 +7) over the music RMS, is gated (-15 to -20 dB before the hit), decays -4 dB at 60 ms, -7 dB at 120 ms, -10 dB at 200 ms, and is bright (centroid 3.4 kHz vs 1.9 kHz for the song). Clip audio is NOT hard-cut at the picture cut (no spectral jump at any of 114 cuts): the cut falls in the quiet gap before the next hit.

Layout: the creator always edits in 16:9. Vertical uploads are that 16:9 master rotated 90 deg clockwise full-frame (3 of 5, including both refs with ~1 M views; verified shot by shot for FB15TNFAHVU) or letterboxed on black (9:16 and 1:1). No centre crop anywhere.

Clip choice is thematic and physical: close-ups of hands/objects producing a crisp transient; HandClap = only hands clapping/snapping, Wellerman = stomps and table bangs, Time Back = clicks/clacks (typewriter, chess, Go stones, gun racks, katana clicks). 11-20 different anime per 10 s, 1-2 shots per anime.

method.downloads: all 6 references downloaded at <= 1080p into C:/Users/Home/AppData/Local/Temp/edit-refs/sound/ (none blocked); the 5 original songs into .../sound/songs/ for alignment
method.frame_analysis: core/edit/refs/sound_analyze.py: every frame at 360 px: luma/contrast/saturation/hue/colourfulness, Laplacian sharpness, frame difference + HSV-histogram Bhattacharyya distance (cuts), linear-blend residual (dissolves), Farneback flow magnitude, LK+RANSAC similarity transform per frame (zoom/rotation/pan/shake), flashes, content box (letterbox); contact sheets of EVERY frame and -4..+4 strips around every detected cut
method.cut_verification: detected cuts checked by eye on the every-frame sheets; flicker inside a shot (flame, explosion flash, eye glint) removed; verified lists in core/edit/refs/sound_timing.py CUTS
method.song_alignment: edit audio vs the original song: onset-envelope cross-correlation over speed 0.70-1.62, chroma check with pitch shifts, sample-accurate lag by waveform correlation, then a +-300 ms lag scan of complex-STFT least-squares subtraction (sharp maximum at 0 ms, 2.8-5.2 dB of energy explained, ~0 elsewhere) -> 4 of 5 references play the original master at speed 1.0, no pitch shift; Time Back uses another master (chroma 0.92 at 39.7 s, no waveform match) and its grid comes from the edit audio
method.clip_sound_layer: edit audio minus the aligned song (complex STFT least squares, 6 bands, 0.25 s windows) = the clips' own sounds; its onsets are the hits; per shot the strongest onset from 2 frames before the cut to 0.45 s after (core/edit/refs/sound_timing.py)
method.layout_check: FB15TNFAHVU vs its own tutorial N1gQySyUGXk (same timing, 16:9 master visible): each vertical frame rotated back 90 deg matches the master exactly (FB15TNFAHVU_rotation_check.png); watermark orientation confirms rotation for qgzBYo7gvhE and jKSxAkOS3JY

tools.timing_vs_song: python core/edit/refs/sound_timing.py ID --ref DIR (needs DIR/analysis/ID.json, ID_audio.json, songs/<song>.m4a, CUTS entry)

timbre_match_song_vs_clip_hit.reading: weak: hits are chosen for crispness and theme, not to imitate the song's instrument

pooled_measurements.spectral_jump_in_clip_audio_at_cut: flux at the cut instant / median flux = 0.67-1.03 (never a spike > 3x at any of 114 cuts): clip audio is not cut with the picture

camera_per_shot.added_shake: none (high shake values only on shots with big source action)

speed.reading: native 24 fps anime timing (on 1s/2s/3s), no interpolation, no ramps

grade_per_reference_shot_medians.reading: source colours; luma p10 of shots 0.13-0.26 (dark shots stay dark); no common tint, no vignette, no grain, no glow

loudness_references.reading: clipped, very loud masters; we keep -14 LUFS / TP < -1 dBTP

style.concept: Each shot = one hit. Pick a percussive 4-bar hook, find the song's hit onsets, and for each hit place a clip whose OWN sound transient lands exactly on it; cut into the clip a short pre-roll earlier. Nothing else moves: the rhythm is carried by the clip sounds and the cut rhythm.

formats.master: render every sound edit as a 16:9 master 1920x1080 (the creator's working format)

short_layouts.name: rot90_cw_full
short_layouts.how: rotate the whole 16:9 master 90 deg clockwise (content top -> right); zero crop; never mix rotated and upright shots in one video

short_layouts.name: letterbox_9x16
short_layouts.how: picture 1080x648 at y=636 on black (n_NvC1IQUMQ measured: the 16:9 master scaled to 1152x648 and 36 px cut off each side); bars stay empty (no blur fill, no text)

short_layouts.name: letterbox_1x1
short_layouts.how: 1080x614 picture at y=234 on black (measured); reference only - our Shorts are 1080x1920

formats.long_form: 1920x1080 is the master itself; the references are Shorts only, so a weekly long video would be a compilation of several sound edits (not observed - see not_observed)

fps.how: 60 fps container with native 24 fps drawings (3:2 repeat), exactly like jKSxAkOS3JY (dup ratio 0.76 at 60 fps); do NOT interpolate

formats.start: t=0 is 50-220 ms before the first hit (the first song onset); the first shot already contains a hit; no title, no fade-in
formats.end: ends after the last shot (10-16 frames) mid-phrase, no fade-out; for a seamless loop reuse the first clip as the last shot (n_NvC1IQUMQ)

structure.song_section: the song's most percussive, recognisable hook: intro riff (Shape of You 0.27 s, Wellerman 1.9 s), chorus (HandClap 28.8 s, Fake 44.5 s, Time Back ~39 s); constant tempo 85-140 BPM; original speed and pitch (speed 1.0000, 0 semitones in 4/4 aligned refs)

optional_intro_shot.when: the percussive part enters after a pickup (qgzBYo7gvhE: 1.25 s before the claps)

structure.energy: no build-up / drop inside a sound edit: cuts per bar constant (+-1); allow +1 cut in the last full bar (2 of 5 refs)
structure.bar_pattern: choose the hit positions of bar 1 from the song, then repeat the same 16th positions in the next bars when the song repeats (target >= 75 % repeat)

hits.detect_song_hits: librosa onset_detect on the ORIGINAL song (hop 128 at 22.05 kHz, backtrack=False, delta 0.12, wait 60 ms) inside the section; strength = onset envelope / its p95; keep onsets with strength >= median of the section

micro_gap.note: 2-3 frame shots only for a double hit (a double clap/knock): 2 of 109 shots are <= 3 frames@24, 4 of 109 are <= 4 frames

hits.grid: hits are real onsets, which sit on the 16th grid (83 % within 30 ms); snap nothing to the grid - align the clip hit to the song onset time itself
hits.coverage: cover about half of the strong song onsets (40-69 %); prefer the ones that repeat each bar and the downbeat/backbeat accents
hits.selection_algorithm: greedy over onsets sorted by strength: accept if >= 0.25 s from accepted hits (or a micro double hit within budget); then fill gaps > 0.6 s with the strongest remaining onset; stop at rate max

cuts.rule: cut_i = hit_i - preroll_i, rounded to the output frame grid; the audio hit is placed sample-accurately at hit_i regardless of the frame grid

preroll_ms.choose: the clip's own wind-up: the frame where the visible motion toward the impact starts, clamped to [50, 290] ms; slower gestures (stomp, table bang) 200-260 ms, clicks/snaps 60-120 ms

cuts.cut_on_beat: do NOT put cuts on song onsets (refs: 10 % within 40 ms); the hit inside the shot is what is on the beat
cuts.visual_sync: the biggest visible change of the shot (impact frame) must fall 1-7 frames@24 after the cut (median 3) and within +-2 frames of the audio hit

camera.note: the Camera from edit_fx must return identity for this style

list.name: cross_dissolve
list.note: FB15TNFAHVU cut 11 (2 frames, out of the intro shot) and cut 90 (3 frames, match-strike glow into brass knuckles: two dark warm shots); use between shots of similar tone, never on the strongest hits

grade.look: neutral: source colours, no LUT, no S-curve, no split toning, no bloom, no grain, no vignette, no letterbox inside the picture
grade.note: the 16:9 master in the tutorial and the published vertical have identical colours; shot-to-shot luma ranges 0.13-0.65, dark shots are left dark

watermark.note: in the rotated layout it rotates with the master (reads top-to-bottom); Latin text only

music.level: constant, untouched, original master, speed 1.0; no ducking (keep gain within +-1 dB)

clip_sounds.source: each shot's own anime audio around its hit (the tutorial shows 2-3 stacked snippets per hit on 3 audio tracks)
clip_sounds.gate: silent (<= -18 dB rel. hit peak) until 10 ms before the hit; 8 ms fade-in; natural decay; 30 ms fade-out ending 25 ms before the next hit or at hit + 0.9 s
clip_sounds.level: hit peak (max 20 ms RMS in the first 120 ms) = music RMS over +-300 ms + 5 dB (allowed +3..+7); whole-shot clip sound RMS between -5 and 0 dB vs music
clip_sounds.eq: high-pass 100 Hz except low hits (stomp/bang/kick-like: low-band share > 0.35); presence +2 dB @ 3.5 kHz Q 1; target centroid 2.3-4.5 kHz
clip_sounds.stacking: a weak hit may be doubled (second copy +0 dB, 0 ms offset) up to 3 layers instead of > +9 dB gain
clip_sounds.overlap: the tail of the previous hit may run into the next shot until the next hit's fade (audio edges independent of picture cuts)
clip_sounds.speech: no words: reject hits with talking within +-0.3 s (tonal low band), allow a short grunt/shout only as the hit itself

audio.no_library_sfx: no risers, whooshes or impacts from a library were detected (no energy at cuts, all hits have matching visible action)

master.stereo: mono-compatible (refs side/mid -7..-20 dB): clip sounds centred, music as is

must: visible physical action that makes a crisp transient: impact, clap, snap, click, clack, knock, stomp, slam, gunshot, gun cock/rack, sword click/clash, cork pop, match strike, typewriter/keys, chess/Go piece
the sound and the visible impact coincide within +-2 frames
close-up or medium close-up of hands / object / feet (about 80 % of shots); faces only as intro/outro stingers or when the face makes the sound
clean frame: no subtitles, no burned-in text, no credits, no watermark of another editor
safe: no blood/gore (drop the knife-into-flesh and finger-cut shots some refs use), no fan service (Monster Musume-type shows excluded), NudeNet + clip_judge as in clip_finder

sound_detector.base: core/meme/align.py sfx_hits on the clip's own audio
sound_detector.calibration: reference hits: flatness p10/50/90 0.12/0.35/0.52, tonal 0.10/0.29/0.44, rise 4.5/11.4/23 dB; the current thresholds (0.18/0.12/6) catch only 62 % of reference hits

clip_selection.theme: when the song title or lyric names a sound (HandClap, Wellerman stomp, Fake gavel), >= 60 % of shots act it out; otherwise mix hit types, weakly matching timbre (low hits on kicks/stomps, bright clicks on hats/marimba; measured correlation only 0.2-0.33)
clip_selection.pool_size: about 3 candidate hit-clips per song hit so each hit can pick the best-fitting pre-roll and sound

hit_sync_cut.what: the core timing of every shot
steps: song hits H (edit time) from the original song section (see style.hits)

for clip j: its audio hits a_j (align.sfx_hits, then refine each to the onset-envelope peak at hop 64 = 2.9 ms) and its visual action frame v_j = argmax of mean |gray_k - gray_{k-1}| in a_j +- 3 frames
assign clips to hits (Hungarian or greedy best score) with score = sfx strength + theme + variety - |v_j - a_j| penalty
preroll_i = clamp(a_j - start of the visible wind-up, 0.05, 0.29) s, default 0.14 s
cut_i = round((H_i - preroll_i) * fps_out) / fps_out; shot i shows clip time t_clip = a_j + (t - H_i) for t in [cut_i, cut_{i+1})
reject a layout where cut_{i+1} - cut_i < 2 source frames or where t_clip leaves the clip (pick a shorter pre-roll or another clip)

native_frames.what: speed 1.0, anime timing untouched, 24 fps drawings in a 60 fps file
native_frames.numpy: k = floor(t_clip * src_fps + 1e-6); frame = cv2.imread(all_paths[k]) - i.e. a ShotFrames(native=True) mode that skips the duplicate-drop and DIS interpolation (ShotFrames.frame would otherwise synthesise in-betweens)

rot90_layout.what: vertical delivery of the 16:9 master (3 of 5 refs)
rot90_layout.rules: rotate every frame (the whole video), including the watermark; no crop, no scale

letterbox_layout.what: 16:9 inside 9:16 on black (1 of 5 refs; 1:1 in another)

cross_dissolve.what: the only soft transition seen: FB15TNFAHVU cut 11 (2 frames: incoming weight 0.35, 0.7) and cut 90 (3 frames: 0.35, 0.6, 0.85); both outgoing and incoming shots keep playing during the mix
cross_dissolve.numpy: n = 2 or 3 source frames; for k in range(n): a = (k+1)/(n+1) (measured 0.35/0.7 and 0.35/0.6/0.85); out = cv2.addWeighted(A[t], 1-a, B[t], a, 0) with A continuing past its cut point; at 60 fps output: n60 = round(n*2.5), a = (k+1)/(n60+1); the incoming hit must still land after the mix ends

hard_cut.numpy: frame switches at cut_i; no flash, no motion blur, no camera punch

clip_audio_gate_and_mix.what: clip hit on top of the untouched song
clip_audio_gate_and_mix.gain: g_i = (music_rms_db(H_i +- 0.3 s) + 5) - hit_peak_db(clip, a_j .. a_j+0.12 s, 20 ms RMS); clamp to [-12, +12] dB; if > +9 dB stack a duplicate instead
clip_audio_gate_and_mix.check: re-run sound_timing.py on the render: hits within 25 ms of song onsets >= 75 %, hit peak over music +3..+7 dB, no spectral spike at cuts

loop_end.how: the last shot is the first clip again (same clip, a later or identical hit), so frame N-1 flows into frame 0; audio: the song section is chosen so that its end + 1 hit returns to the first hit's bar position

watermark.what: faint creator tag on the master
watermark.pil: draw 'ZeroYenOtaku' in an italic Latin font, cap height 0.025*1080 px, white, alpha 0.3, centred at (0.45*1920, 0.07*1080) on the 16:9 master before rotation

quality_targets.measure_with: sound_analyze.py (every frame) + sound_timing.py (song alignment is exact because we render the song ourselves: pass our own song window as the 'aligned' song)

targets.frame_checks: no subtitle/text band (edit_fx.text_band == 0), no blood/red-liquid dominated frames, no NudeNet hits

not_observed.note: things the owner may expect from other groups that these 6 sound-edit references do NOT use; keep them out of the sound-edit pipeline or mark them as our own extension
items: split-screen, postcard or frame layouts, 3D tilts
long-form 16:9 uploads (all six are Shorts; a long-form sound-edit compilation would be our own extension: several 10 s sound edits of different songs joined with hard cuts on the song change)
